benchmarks.name: OSWorld 2.0
benchmarks.measures: Long-horizon desktop computer use: an agent drives a real Ubuntu desktop to finish multi-step tasks scored against checkpoints.
benchmarks.notes: Binary completion = share of tasks where every checkpoint passed; partial score credits individual checkpoints, so the two columns are not interchangeable. Runs use the 500-step budget unless stated.

benchmarks.name: WorkArena++
benchmarks.measures: Knowledge-worker tasks inside ServiceNow: list filtering, form filling, ordering and cross-module reasoning.
benchmarks.notes: No clean continuously maintained public result file; benchmark metadata is official, scores come from vendor/paper runs and are not a single unified leaderboard.

benchmarks.name: EnterpriseOps-Gym
benchmarks.measures: Realistic enterprise operations workflows, including tool retrieval versus oracle tool access and feasibility/refusal handling.
benchmarks.notes: Keep the benchmark-owner run distinct from the EnterpriseOps-Gym-AA/Stirrup reimplementation; preserve tool-retrieval mode (oracle vs distractor) because it materially changes scores.

benchmarks.name: WebArena-Verified
benchmarks.measures: Self-hosted web navigation across shopping, CMS, GitLab, maps and forums, with verified task data and evaluators.
benchmarks.notes: Original WebArena results are not interchangeable with WebArena-Verified; the Hard subset and evaluator protocol must be preserved. Harness is typically BrowserGym.

benchmarks.name: WebChoreArena
benchmarks.measures: Repetitive, tedious and memory-intensive web chores that go beyond simple navigation.
benchmarks.notes: Official leaderboard is a Google Sheet, which is a weaker machine source than a checked-in JSON; results should be re-verified against pinned sheet tabs.

benchmarks.name: SpreadsheetBench 2
benchmarks.measures: Deliverable-level spreadsheet work on large multi-sheet workbooks.
benchmarks.notes: Preserve task category and agent scaffold; results are only comparable at the same scaffold.

benchmarks.name: AA-AnalystAgent
benchmarks.measures: Long-horizon analyst work: finding, reconciling and reporting on data to produce a deliverable.
benchmarks.notes: Task set is private, so this is an independent/private benchmark rather than a fully reproducible public one. pass@1, pass@5 and pass^5 are separate metrics; pass^5 is the reliability headline.

benchmarks.name: AA-Briefcase
benchmarks.measures: Professional deliverable production (briefs, decks) judged on rubric pass rate and head-to-head quality.
benchmarks.notes: Rubric pass rate, analytical-quality Elo, presentation Elo and the combined AA-Briefcase Elo are distinct metrics and must not be collapsed into one percentage.

benchmarks.name: GDPval-AA v2
benchmarks.measures: Agentic implementation of GDPval: real occupation deliverables judged pairwise for quality.
benchmarks.notes: Independent agentic implementation of OpenAI's GDPval, not the same protocol as OpenAI's original evaluation.

benchmarks.name: AutomationBench
benchmarks.measures: End-to-end workflow automation across real SaaS apps, from a short business request.
benchmarks.notes: Three distinct protocols exist: Zapier's harder held-out leaderboard, runs on the public GitHub task set, and Artificial Analysis' AutomationBench-AA. Public tasks differ from the held-out set, so scores across these must never be merged.

benchmarks.name: APEX-Agents
benchmarks.measures: Professional-services tasks in realistic investment-banking, consulting and law workflows.
benchmarks.notes: "APEX-Agents" without a dataset revision is insufficient: task/world counts changed between public releases. Preserve harness, reasoning effort and run date.

benchmarks.name: Agents' Last Exam
benchmarks.measures: Expert-level multi-step reasoning and research tasks, scored on full completion and partial credit.
benchmarks.notes: Full-completion/pass rate and partial score are separate metrics and must not be collapsed. Reference/ground-truth data is gated, so third-party protocols can diverge sharply.

benchmarks.name: Toolathlon-Verified
benchmarks.measures: Realistic tool-use workflows with automated verification and public trajectories.
benchmarks.notes: Use the Verified release identity and retain model+harness details. Different leaderboards report different subsets (full verified set versus a 100-task subset), which are not interchangeable.

benchmarks.name: CRMArena-Pro
benchmarks.measures: CRM tasks across B2B/B2C and interactive/non-interactive splits, including privacy-aware responses.
benchmarks.notes: Distinguish B2B/B2C and interactive/non-interactive splits. Public benchmark data is cleaner than continuously updated public result data, so newer scores need the curated manual-result path.

benchmarks.name: TheAgentCompany
benchmarks.measures: A simulated software company where an agent completes real tasks across GitLab, ownCloud, Plane and RocketChat.
benchmarks.notes: Versioned result tree with per-run task-level JSON, screenshots and trajectories is the best-practice provenance pattern. Full completion and partial completion are separate metrics.

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench 2.1
benchmarks.measures: Terminal-native tasks an agent must complete end-to-end from a shell.
benchmarks.notes: Submissions pin the dataset and require public Harbor jobs, agent, model, reasoning effort and repeated trials. Terminal-Bench 2.0, 2.1, 3.0 and older beta/core are distinct protocols.

benchmarks.name: AppWorld
benchmarks.measures: Controllable apps (email, Spotify-like, shopping) driven through APIs to complete everyday and complex tasks.
benchmarks.notes: Primary automated source is the leaderboard repo's raw _leaderboard.json with per-experiment bundles retained for provenance.

benchmarks.name: τ³-bench
benchmarks.measures: Multi-turn tool + policy adherence with a simulated user, across domains like airline, retail, telecom and banking.
benchmarks.notes: τ / τ² / τ³ are distinct generations; τ³ knowledge/voice results are not comparable with older τ² text-domain scores. Preserve domain, split, pass@k, modality, user-simulator version and retrieval config.

benchmarks.name: BrowseComp
benchmarks.measures: Hard-to-find factual questions that require browsing and reasoning to answer.
benchmarks.notes: simple-evals is the OpenAI reference implementation but is deprecated for new results; newest BrowseComp scores come from vendor cards or reproducible runs and use the manual-result path.

benchmarks.name: OSWorld-Verified
benchmarks.measures: The verified revision of the original OSWorld desktop benchmark.
benchmarks.notes: Kept separate from original OSWorld and OSWorld 2.0; public verified trajectories are available.

benchmarks.name: MCPMark Verified
benchmarks.measures: Reproducible real MCP workflows across Notion, GitHub, Filesystem, Postgres and Playwright with automated verifiers.
benchmarks.notes: MCPMark Verified is the default; earlier task versions are deprecated and non-comparable.

benchmarks.name: MCP-Atlas
benchmarks.measures: Tool use across 36 version-pinned real MCP servers with 307 tools.
benchmarks.notes: Scoring is LLM-as-judge, so the judge model/version matters for comparability.

benchmarks.name: τ²-bench
benchmarks.measures: The τ² generation of multi-turn tool + policy tasks; retained as a historical protocol.
benchmarks.notes: Historical protocol; do not compare directly with τ³ results.

metrics.label: Binary completion
metrics.description: Share of tasks where every scoring checkpoint passed.

metrics.label: Partial score
metrics.description: Mean share of scoring checkpoints reached, even when the task was not finished.

metrics.label: Accuracy
metrics.description: Share of tasks answered or completed correctly.

metrics.label: Resolved
metrics.description: Share of software-engineering issues resolved against the test suite.

metrics.label: Full completion
metrics.description: Binary share of tasks with all checkpoints passed.

metrics.label: Partial completion
metrics.description: Weighted progress score that credits checkpoints plus a full-completion bonus.

metrics.label: Elo
metrics.description: Preference-based rating from paired head-to-head judging.

metrics.label: Tool invocation rate
metrics.description: Share of tasks where the agent actually invoked the required tool.
